name: 6.5 V12 NA
notes: Variant: Ferrari 812 Superfast (type F152 BC; Swiss/EU type approvals 2017-2021, US model years 2018-2021; F140 GA 6,496 cc 65-degree V12, 588 kW / 800 cv at 8,500 rpm, 8,900 rpm maximum engine speed) with the 7-speed F1 dual-clutch transmission in the rear transaxle (front-mid engine, rear-wheel drive), on the standard rear 315/35 ZR20 tyre (driven axle; front 275/35 ZR20). Gearbox: no Ferrari or type-approval document listing the per-gear ratios was found (Ferrari's press release and its model pages for the 812 Superfast, 812 GTS, 812 Competizione, F12berlinetta and 12Cilindri give none; the US EPA and Swiss ASTRA data give only the axle ratio), nor a variant of this car/engine with primary-sourced ratios, so the gear ratios 3.34/2.29/1.73/1.37/1.11/0.90/0.70 come from auto motor und sport's technical data for its 812 Superfast test car (secondary press, two decimals) - flagged; replace them if a Ferrari or type-approval document with the ratios is found. Final drive: the US EPA Test Car List gives axle 4.37 for the 812 Superfast (MY2018-2021; also for the F12 Berlinetta) and 4.38 for the 812 GTS and 812 Competizione, and every Swiss federal type approval of the 812 (and F12) in ASTRA's TARGA data gives iA 4,38; 4.375 (= 35/8, consistent with both two-decimal figures) is used, so overall ratio = gear x 4.375. EPA N/V cross-check: 7th (0.70 x 4.375 = 3.0625) on 315/35ZR20 gives 37.00 rpm/mph vs the EPA 36.2 (+2.2 %, inside the 2.5 % tolerance); the EPA figure alone would imply a 7th of about 0.685, slightly taller than the secondary 0.70 (the EPA F12 Berlinetta row, same 4.37 axle and 315/35 ZR20 rear tyre, N/V 36.9, implies 0.698). The EPA 812 GTS and 812 Competizione rows (axle 4.38, N/V 36.2) belong to other variants and are not used. Combustion: 65-degree V12 (Ferrari); entries listed in firing order at an even 720/12 = 60-degree interval with banks strictly alternating; bank 0 = the bank of the cylinder that fires first, bank 1 = the other bank (Ferrari's cylinder numbering was not verified). Neither the firing order nor the crankpin arrangement was found in a Ferrari document: the even 60-degree interval assumes crankpins phased for even firing; with six common crankpins (two rods per pin) a 65-degree vee would instead fire at alternating 65/55-degree intervals (0, 65, 120, 185, 240, 305, 360, 425, 480, 545, 600, 665) - revisit if a Ferrari source is found. Any bank-alternating firing order gives the same angle/bank data. RPM: redline and limiter at the published 8,900 rpm maximum engine speed (Ferrari's 812 GTS page calls it the '8900 rpm rev limit'; same F140 GA engine); the 812 Superfast page text also speaks of power rising 'all the way to the maximum revs of 8,500 rpm', which is the power peak, not the rev limit. Estimated (not published in the sources used): idle 850 rpm; limiter type fuel-soft with 150 rpm hysteresis; shift time 0.10 s (DCT default).
